articles.title: Swapping Jolt's sorted collections to a B+tree
articles.summary: Swapping Jolt's sorted collections to a B+tree has been accomplished by updating Jolt's sorted collections along with the java.util.TreeMap and TreeSet shims to use a persistent B+tree, which has dropped peak memory by 40% while making most operations faster at every size. The B+tree's layout, which keeps data in leaves of up to 16 entries and branches through inner nodes of up to 32 children, has also improved memory use, with a full leaf holding 16 entries in 34 machine words and a worst-case scenario of 34 bytes per entry. This has resulted in a significant reduction in memory usage, with a full leaf now needing only 17 bytes per entry against the red-black tree's 48.
